# The words an ask may use

How a sound should be, in the words a person would use. These are what a
ToneSpec's `words` field carries, and the only ones it carries: a word outside
this list is reported and moves nothing, rather than being refused, because
refusing an ask over a word would make the format hostile to the person it
exists for.

24 words on 10 axes. 6 of those axes move a control when a preset is built and 4
describe the player and the instrument, which no amplifier, reverb or compressor
has a control for.

## Describe the result, not the control

"mid-forward", never "raise the mids". Where the treble knob sits is a fact
about somebody's amplifier; how the record came out is a fact about the sound,
and only the second survives being read on other gear. That is why a knob
position is never written in an ask.

## One word per axis

An axis is a question, and the words on it are answers that exclude each other.
Saying `mid-forward` has already said `not scooped`, so an ask claiming both has
claimed nothing: apply them in turn and the control lands where it started. A
build reports an axis answered twice and moves neither.

A word that would answer two axes at once cannot be written yet. "Punchy" is the
obvious one, meaning both a bottom that stops when the note does and a front of
the note you can hear. Nothing structural forbids it. What is missing is how to
divide one word's step between two controls, and nobody has measured that.

## Evidence decides how far a word moves

A word carries its own evidence, and that is not decoration. How far it moves a
control is sized from how far that word's own measurement sits from every other
rig's, so a word measured close to the pack barely moves anything and a word
nobody measured takes the whole step. It is the difference between a knob moved
because somebody listened and a knob moved because a model guessed.

One word is one opinion, so no word moves a control more than a quarter of its
range whatever its evidence says.

## attack

what the front of a note sounds like

| word | means | moves |
| ---- | ----- | ----- |
| `audible-pick-attack` | the pick is a sound of its own, not just a way in | Attack half a step up on the comp |
| `percussive` | the string against the fretboard is part of the sound | Attack up on the comp |
| `soft-attack` | notes arrive rather than start | Attack down on the comp |

## decay

how long a note lasts once it is struck

Nothing on this axis moves a control. It is recorded because two rigs on the
same amplifier read as different sounds, and because a figure measured from a
record should not be read as the amplifier's doing.

| word | means |
| ---- | ----- |
| `long-decay` | notes ring on and overlap |
| `short-decay` | notes stop, whether from the hands or the strings |

## drive

how hard the amplifier is being pushed

| word | means | moves |
| ---- | ----- | ----- |
| `clean` | no breakup at any dynamic | Drive down on the amp |
| `grit-on-attack` | the front of the note breaks up and the body does not | Drive half a step up on the amp |
| `minimal-drive` | breakup only where it is played hardest | Drive half a step down on the amp |
| `saturated` | breakup throughout, part of the voice rather than an accent | Drive up on the amp |

## highs

the top, and how much of it there is

| word | means | moves |
| ---- | ----- | ----- |
| `bright` | top open, the attack audible | Treble up on the amp |
| `dark` | top rolled off, tone knob down | Treble down on the amp |
| `glassy` | top open and hard, closer to a bell than a growl | Treble up on the amp |

## low-end

how the bottom behaves, not how much of it there is

| word | means | moves |
| ---- | ----- | ----- |
| `loose-low-end` | the bottom blooms and hangs on | Sag up on the amp |
| `tight-low-end` | the bottom stops when the note does | Sag down on the amp |

## mids

where the middle of the range sits

| word | means | moves |
| ---- | ----- | ----- |
| `mid-forward` | mids pushed, the part sits in front of the mix | Mid up on the amp |
| `scooped` | mids pulled, the part sits under everything else | Mid down on the amp |

## movement

whether the tone stays put while a note lasts

Nothing on this axis moves a control. It is recorded because two rigs on the
same amplifier read as different sounds, and because a figure measured from a
record should not be read as the amplifier's doing.

| word | means |
| ---- | ----- |
| `envelope-swept` | a filter follows the note, so the vowel changes as it decays |
| `static` | the tone is the same at the end of a note as at the start |

## pickup

where along the string the sound is taken from

Nothing on this axis moves a control. It is recorded because two rigs on the
same amplifier read as different sounds, and because a figure measured from a
record should not be read as the amplifier's doing.

| word | means |
| ---- | ----- |
| `bridge-forward` | nasal and hard, fundamental pulled back |
| `neck-forward` | round and full, harmonics pulled back |

## space

what surrounds the part

| word | means | moves |
| ---- | ----- | ----- |
| `dry` | no room on it | Mix down on the reverb |
| `roomy` | an audible space around the part | Mix up on the reverb |

## string-noise

what the hands make that is not a note

Nothing on this axis moves a control. It is recorded because two rigs on the
same amplifier read as different sounds, and because a figure measured from a
record should not be read as the amplifier's doing.

| word | means |
| ---- | ----- |
| `audible-strings` | the hands moving is part of what you hear |
| `quiet-strings` | little finger noise, usually flatwounds |

## Where this comes from

`pkg/sdk/internal/compile/data/words.json` holds the axes and the definitions,
and `pkg/sdk/internal/compile/move.go` holds what each word moves. This page is
generated from both, so it cannot fall behind either.
